doc.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 17, 2022 [interview 2 of 2]

title: How Sun Ra's band members made a living
summary: Band members came from Chicago and worked other jobs such as Broadway shows and Art Blakey; Sun Ra promised fame rather than money.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I may have a misconception about the group and how they operated, but is there enough to see how did those members of that group actually make a living? Were they making enough money to pay rent and eat?

At that time, see Sun Ra, he got there in ’58. I got there in 1960. He brought all his members from Chicago, mainly Ronnie Boykins, the bass player; Pat Patrick was the baritone saxophone player; Marshall Allen, alto; John Gilmore, tenor; and was using Clifford Jarvis on the drums and Lex Humphries. He had another drummer, it might have been Phil Grant, I’m not sure, from Chicago. But I worked with him with Lex Humphries you know. And no, all these guys, they were great musicians so that enabled them to work shows. Like Pat Patrick would work Broadway shows and theaters. Like I say, Gilmore had — took a gig with Art Blakey you know. And all these guys was working

the New York scene as well as with Sun Ra. And Sun Ra would say, “Well I’m not going to pay — there’s not going to be that much money but you will become famous if you work with me.” I said, “Really?” Well he could talk. I mean he was a salesman, constantly selling. I mean he was really, his ideology, he was very astute, very articulate when it came to expressing ideas and whatnot. You know, and telling stories. Sometimes the rehearsal would go on just listening to his stories, to give you a concept.
